description: Declaration of Elephant Corridors in Monaragala and Hambantota Districts to minimize human-elephant conflicts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Wild elephants live in about 2/3 of the country's land area, and the rapid blockage of wild elephant habitats and migration routes due to various development projects and human activities has directly affected the escalation of elephant-human conflicts. It has been identified that the protection of wild elephant habitats and migration routes should be done urgently to minimize such conflicts to some extent. The Department of Wildlife Conservation, in collaboration with the relevant Divisional Secretaries, stakeholder institutions and organizations, is currently identifying the migration routes of wild elephants. Under the programme to identify wild elephant migration routes in the Monaragala District, the wild elephant migration route from Handapanagala to the Yala National Park via the Menik River in Demodara has been identified, and the approval for the same has also been received from the Monaragala District Coordination Committee. The elephant migration route from Lunugamvehera National Park in Zone VI of the Yala National Park to Udawalawe National Park was declared as the Wetahira Kanda Wildlife Sanctuary in the year 2002. 05 plots of land with land permits have been identified in the relevant area, and these lands have not been developed yet. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take the following steps, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	To declare the elephant migration route from Handapanagala in the Monaragala District to the Yala National Park via the Menik River in Demodara as a sanctuary under the provisions of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance.

*	To re-declare the Watahira Kanda Nature Reserve as a 'Forest Gateway' by providing alternative lands at a suitable location outside the wildlife reserve, instead of 05 plots of land with land permits located within the Watahira Kanda Nature Reserve Area.

*	To acquire the plots of land including the buildings constructed blocking the Koholankala Elephant corridor in the Hambantota District by paying compensation and declare the area belonging to the Hambantota Wild Elephant Management Reserve as a sanctuary.
